samples.summary: New model-level mutators `Sheet.changeDecimals` / `Sheet.unsetRangeStyleKeys` carry no read-only or permission gate of their own; enforcement lives only in the two view-layer callers (`Spreadsheet.increaseDecimals`/`decreaseDecimals`, packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:535,545). I traced every call site and both are still guarded by `if (!this.sheet || this._readOnly) return;`, so this change does not weaken the existing gate — but it moves the write logic (store.set/delete, setSheetStyle, setColumnStyle, setRowStyle, setRangeStyles) one layer further from the only place the read-only flag is checked, and `unsetRangeStyleKeys` is now a public API any future caller can reach unguarded. Note that read-only here is a client-side UI concept only; document-level authorization is enforced server-side outside this package, so the impact is limited to a local UI-state bypass, not a server-side authorization bypass.
searchedFor: Grep 'changeDecimals|unsetRangeStyleKeys|getActiveDecimalState|increaseDecimals|decreaseDecimals' repo-wide (only spreadsheet.ts + tests + docs call them)
Grep 'protect|locked|isProtected|permission' in packages/sheets/src/model (no model-level permission concept exists)
Read Sheet.setRangeStyle (sheet.ts:3695) — same absence of a model-level gate, so this is consistent with the pre-existing design
samples.evidence: Vector: any caller of the newly public `Sheet.unsetRangeStyleKeys(keys)` / `Sheet.changeDecimals(delta)` performs persistent style writes (sheet.ts:4285 setSheetStyle, :4296 setColumnStyle, :4308 setRowStyle, :4330 setRangeStyles, :4368-4370 store.delete/set) without consulting any read-only flag. I could not complete an exploit chain: the only current callers (packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:535 and :545) both check `this._readOnly` before delegating, and no frontend code calls the Sheet methods directly (packages/frontend/src/components/formatting-toolbar.tsx:249,253 go through Spreadsheet). Hence low confidence / minor — a latent-gap note, not a live bypass.

samples.summary: `removeCellStyleKeysInRange` rewrites each affected cell as `compactCell(existing, next)`, and `compactCell` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/style-mutation.ts:57) reconstructs the cell from only `v`, `f` and `s` — any other persisted Cell fields on that record (e.g. spill metadata such as `spillRows`/`spillCols`/`spillBlocked`, see packages/sheets/src/model/core/types.ts:216) are silently dropped when the decimal keys are removed. This is data destruction on a shared collaborative document triggered by a formatting button, i.e. an integrity concern rather than an access-control one; the deeper correctness analysis belongs to the correctness lens and I defer the final call there.
searchedFor: Grep 'compactCell' call sites in sheet.ts to check the pattern is pre-existing
samples.evidence: An editor selects a range containing a spill anchor and clicks Decrease decimals once too often; `unsetRangeStyleKeys` reaches sheet.ts:4366 and writes back `compactCell(existing, next)`, which keeps only v/f/s and therefore erases the anchor's spill bookkeeping fields for every collaborator on the document. I confirmed compactCell's field whitelist but did not confirm that a spill anchor can co-exist with a `dp`/`nf` style key in practice, hence medium confidence.
